semantics.what: A FastAPI order-taking service: accepts orders on a public HTTP API, prices them, persists them, and charges a card.
semantics.how: Six semantic layers. Requests enter through a rate-limited, token-authenticated router, drop into the orders domain, and fan out to Postgres and Stripe.
semantics.when: Per inbound HTTP request; migrations and scripts run out-of-band.
semantics.where: One deployable process plus Redis and Postgres.
semantics.why: Sells things. Everything else in the tree exists to make that request path correct, bounded, and observable.

semantics.what: Order lifecycle and the money that makes it real.
semantics.how: create_order prices, persists, charges, and compensates on failure; get_order reads.
semantics.when: Downstream of the edge layer, never called directly.
semantics.why: The only place business rules are allowed to live.

semantics.what: Everything that touches an untrusted request before the domain sees it.
semantics.how: FastAPI router with two dependencies in order — rate limit, then token auth.
semantics.why: One place where admission control lives, so a policy change is one diff and not a grep.

semantics.what: Database access and process settings.
semantics.how: Thin async query helpers; environment-backed settings object read at import.
semantics.when: DB on every persisted operation; config once at boot.
semantics.why: Keeps connection and environment concerns out of domain code.

semantics.what: Structured logging and a domain event emitter.
semantics.how: structlog logger; emit() is still a stub.
semantics.why: Cross-cutting concerns that would otherwise be copy-pasted.

semantics.what: Unit tests for the limiter, integration tests for orders.
semantics.how: pytest.
semantics.why: Coverage of the limiter is good; coverage of the wiring is not.

semantics.what: Single-order read.
semantics.how: Same guard chain, then one indexed lookup.
semantics.why: The guard chain authenticates but does not authorise: any valid token can read any order id.

semantics.what: The write path from public HTTP to a charged, persisted order.
semantics.how: Two router dependencies, then six sequential domain steps.
semantics.why: Every hop is blocking and none of them has a timeout. The path touches Redis, Postgres, and Stripe in series, so its tail latency is the sum of three external systems.

semantics.what: The public route table. Two endpoints: POST /public/orders, GET /public/orders/{id}.
semantics.how: APIRouter with prefix /public and two Depends() — rate_limit("public") then verify_token.
semantics.when: Import time builds the table; per-request the dependency chain runs.
semantics.why: A single declaration of what is publicly reachable and what guards it.

semantics.what: Bearer-style token check against a hard-coded set.
semantics.how: Reads x-api-token, raises 401 if absent or unknown.
semantics.when: Second dependency on every public route.
semantics.why: Minimum viable identity. The in-memory token set is a fixture, not a design.

semantics.what: Membership test against a module-level set.
semantics.how: token in _KNOWN_TOKENS.
semantics.why: Fixture-grade. A real store goes behind this one function.

semantics.what: Rejects requests without a known token.
semantics.how: Header lookup, then a set membership test.
semantics.when: After the rate limiter, on every public request.
semantics.why: Runs second, so unauthenticated traffic is rate-limited before it is rejected — an anonymous flood consumes the anon bucket, not the auth path.

semantics.what: Process settings read from the environment at import.
semantics.how: Class attributes, with a nested rate_limit block added by RL-114.
semantics.why: Fails loudly at boot on a missing variable rather than quietly at request time.

semantics.what: Port, database URL, and the nested rate-limit block.
semantics.how: os.environ at class-body evaluation — a missing DATABASE_URL or RATE_LIMIT_REDIS_URL raises at import.
semantics.why: public_per_min was lowered from 100 to 60 by hand after a capacity review. The inline comment is the only record of that reasoning anywhere in the repository.

semantics.what: Async query helpers.
semantics.how: execute/fetch_one, both NotImplementedError.
semantics.why: One seam for pooling and instrumentation later.

semantics.what: The write path: parse, price, insert, charge, emit, respond 201.
semantics.how: On a failed charge it deletes the row it just wrote and raises 402.
semantics.why: The compensating delete is the only consistency mechanism. If the process dies between insert and charge, the row survives unpaid and nothing reconciles it.

semantics.what: Handler for order creation.
semantics.how: parse → price → insert → charge → emit → 201; rollback + 402 on charge failure.
semantics.why: Six sequential steps with one compensating branch. The emit at the end is a no-op, so a confirmed order publishes nothing.

semantics.what: Request body validation.
semantics.how: NotImplementedError.
semantics.why: Placeholder — the 400 branch is currently unreachable.

semantics.what: Read path for a single order.
semantics.how: repo.find_order, 404 on None.
semantics.why: No ownership check beyond the router dependency — any valid token reads any order.

semantics.what: Line-item pricing.
semantics.how: Sums unit_price × qty in one generator expression.
semantics.why: Float arithmetic on money, and no currency field. Both will have to change.

semantics.what: Order persistence: insert, find, hard delete.
semantics.how: Inline SQL through the db connection helpers.
semantics.why: rollback() is a hard delete, so a failed payment leaves no audit trail of the attempt.

semantics.what: Card charges via Stripe.
semantics.how: charge() delegates to a stripe_client that is still NotImplementedError.
semantics.when: Once per created order, after the row is written.
semantics.why: Isolates the third-party SDK behind one function so the domain never imports Stripe.

semantics.what: The Stripe call surface, plus an unrouted webhook handler.
semantics.how: Both NotImplementedError.
semantics.why: No timeout, retry, or idempotency key is planned yet, and handle_webhook is orphaned — nothing in the tree routes to it.

semantics.what: Domain event emitter.
semantics.how: emit(name, *args) — a stub.
semantics.why: Placeholder for an outbox. create_order believes it published order.confirmed. It did not.

semantics.what: A structlog logger and one request-logging helper.
semantics.how: Emits request_id, route, duration_ms as structured fields.
semantics.when: Per request and inside the limiter.
semantics.why: The field names are a contract with log parsers that live outside this repository. The analyzer cannot see them, so it cannot confirm the rename was safe.

semantics.what: Legacy in-process throttle keyed by a per-instance dict.
semantics.how: Counters in local memory, no shared state.
semantics.why: Superseded — it could not bound a client spread across instances.

semantics.what: Three integration tests over the order path.
semantics.how: 201 on create, 404 on missing, rollback on charge failure.
semantics.when: CI — but not re-run since the routing change.
semantics.why: These are the only tests that would catch the limiter breaking the order path, and they are stale.
